environment.browser: Codex in-app browser, after user restarted Codex
environment.adapter: ANGLE (AMD, ANGLE Metal Renderer: AMD Radeon Pro 560X, Unspecified Version)
environment.physics: CPU multigrid-PCG and WebAssembly surface contacts; GPU transport, air textures, fine particles and rendering

change: Allow up to ten seconds to observe completion of each isolated one-pixel startup draw. Normal scene frames and previously queued simulation work retain their two-second completion budget. No concurrent frames or automatic retries were added.

evidence.initialFailure: First-use completion timed out at opaque-reflection-lighting without context loss; initial-playback-timeout.json. A subsequent attempt before the fix progressed to opaque-lighting and timed out there instead.
evidence.isolatedFirstUse: first-use.json contains two sequential one-pixel draws of reflection lighting and water lighting. Earlier attempts may have warmed the driver cache.
evidence.smallPlayback: 24-step and 120-step playback passed at 96 x 64, with glass spawning halfway, 44 stable prepared programs and no context loss. See playback-24.json and playback-120.json.
evidence.normalBeach: Normal live beach at 2.2x resolution, 110 m width, 24 m/s wind and adaptive rendering completed 45 frames. Then a fresh normal scene with a spawned glass ball completed another 45 frames. Viewport 1280 x 720, drawing scale 50%. See normal-beach-45.json and normal-beach-object-45.json.
evidence.visual: normal-beach.jpg shows the normal beach paused after successful playback with the spawned glass sphere. No error/warning console messages were captured at completion.
evidence.interruptedAttempt: One intervening object benchmark was interrupted by Vite reloading after an unrelated diagnostic-file edit. It is excluded from successful-run counts.

tests.command: node --test tests/live-*.test.js tests/rtx-*.test.js tests/beach-fields*.test.js tests/fluid-fields*.test.js tests/webgpu-pressure-probe.test.js

evidence.build: npm run build passed; existing chunk-size warning remains

limitations: These are bounded playback and visual checks, not a long-duration stability guarantee or fully cold-driver-cache validation.
Normal playback remains slow on this GPU: about 2.8 FPS and 0.18x realtime in the measured runs. High paused FPS is not playback throughput.
The completion guard cannot preempt an individual draw or synchronous driver compilation. This change adjusts startup observation, not GPU execution limits.
No GPU pressure backend or WebGPU beach solver was enabled by these checks. Windows/RTX was not retested on hardware.
